problem: Text embedding models vary in performance across domains and tasks, and existing ensemble methods cannot effectively leverage model-specific uncertainty, limiting their robustness.
approach: Transform deterministic embeddings into probabilistic ones post-hoc, then compute adaptive ensemble coefficients based on embedding uncertainty using a principled surrogate-loss formulation and an uncertainty-aware similarity function.
contribution: UEC consistently improves both performance and robustness across diverse benchmarks by combining principled uncertainty modeling with ensemble learning.

problem: Standard imitation learning only matches expert expected returns but ignores risk attitudes and other distributional features, failing to capture the full behavioral profile.
approach: Formulate risk-sensitive IL as return distribution matching in Wasserstein distance, introduce non-Markovian policies for expressivity, and develop two algorithms (RS-BC and RS-KT) with theoretical sample complexity guarantees.
contribution: RS-KT achieves substantially lower sample complexity than RS-BC by exploiting dynamics information, with provably efficient algorithms for both known and unknown reward settings.

problem: Fine-tuning flow and diffusion models for reward optimization is memory-intensive and scales poorly, while existing methods like Classifier Guidance lack expressivity and suffer distribution mismatch.
approach: Learn a value function within an optimal control setting with flexible value network complexity, enabling on-policy optimization of non-differentiable rewards while controlling memory and compute demands.
contribution: Value Matching achieves comparable performance to full fine-tuning methods while requiring less than 5% of their memory usage, with improved stability and sample efficiency.

problem: Bird's-eye view representations lose detail and limit feature alignment in multi-modal sensor fusion, leading to ineffective multi-task perception.
approach: Use 3D Gaussian representation to unify multi-modal features in continuous space, with a forward-projection-based initialization module and shared cross-modal Gaussian encoder using attention-based updates.
contribution: GaussianFusion outperforms BEVFusion by 2.6 NDS on nuScenes 3D object detection and surpasses GaussFormer on semantic occupancy with 1.55 mIoU improvement while achieving 450% speedup.

problem: Designing images that consistently elicit desired neural responses is difficult due to noisy EEG signals, non-differentiable feedback, and lack of explicit reward models.
approach: Use closed-loop optimization with EEG signals as feedback to guide naturalistic image generation, treating the brain as a black-box function with pseudo-model guidance for iterative refinement.
contribution: MindPilot enables efficient semantic target retrieval, closed-loop EEG feature optimization, and human-subject validation in mental matching and emotion regulation tasks.

problem: Standard RL for LLMs struggles to escape local optima of pre-trained policies, boosting single-solution accuracy at the expense of solution diversity and multi-solution performance.
approach: Adopt a risk-seeking objective interpolating between mean and maximum rewards, derive Risk-Sensitive GRPO that emphasizes hard prompts to drive exploration.
contribution: RS-GRPO consistently improves pass@k performance across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and five LLMs while enhancing or maintaining pass@1.

problem: Test-time adaptation methods rely on backpropagation, which is memory and computation intensive for resource-constrained devices and often tied to specific architectures.
approach: Analyze domain shift as three embedding-space distortions (translation, scaling, rotation) and correct them via backpropagation-free covariance alignment at each intermediate layer with only two forward passes.
contribution: PEA achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency while proving versatile across ViTs and CNNs without requiring backpropagation.

problem: Unsupervised cross-modal flow estimation faces challenges from modality discrepancy and geometric misalignment without ground-truth flow labels.
approach: Use decoupled optimization with task-specific supervision for modality transfer and flow estimation networks, combined with geometry-aware data synthesis and cross-modal consistency constraints.
contribution: DCFlow integrates with various flow estimation networks and achieves state-of-the-art performance among unsupervised approaches on cross-modal flow benchmarks.

problem: Generating realistic human-object interaction animations requires jointly modeling dynamic actions and diverse geometries while maintaining contact quality without handcrafted priors.
approach: Factor representation into modality-specific components with individualized noise levels and asynchronous denoising schedules, enabling guidance through cross-attention without classifiers.
contribution: This data-driven approach achieves higher contact fidelity, more realistic HOI generation, and stronger generalization to unseen objects and tasks than conventional classifier-free guidance.

problem: Using static images for reward shaping loses dynamic motion information and single viewpoints occlude critical behavior aspects, while linear addition of VLM scores can alter optimal policy.
approach: Model task relevance using multi-view videos with video-text similarity from frozen VLMs, learn a state relevance function, and apply state-dependent reward shaping that reduces VLM influence once behavior matches.
contribution: MVR demonstrates efficacy on HumanoidBench locomotion and MetaWorld manipulation with improved performance verified through ablation studies.

problem: Existing 3DGS relighting methods use coarse shading decompositions, limiting fidelity and physical interpretability for anisotropic metals and translucent materials.
approach: Decompose reflectance into four components (diffuse, specular, shadow, subsurface scattering) with learnable dipole-based scattering, occlusion-aware shadows, and anisotropic Fresnel-based specular.
contribution: SSD-GS achieves superior relighting quality on OLAT datasets while enabling controllable light editing and interactive scene relighting with improved physical interpretability.

problem: Flow matching models lack temporal structure awareness in GRPO training, with uniform credit assignment failing to capture varying decision criticality across generation timesteps.
approach: Introduce trajectory branching for process rewards at designated points, noise-aware weighting modulating by timestep exploration potential, and seed grouping to control initialization effects.
contribution: TempFlow-GRPO achieves state-of-the-art human preference alignment in text-to-image generation by capturing temporal structure in flow-based generation.

problem: Standard policy learning assumes unconfoundedness, producing biased estimates when unobserved confounding exists, potentially leading to harmful policies.
approach: Employ causal sensitivity analysis to derive a semi-parametrically efficient estimator for sharp bounds on value functions under unobserved confounding, avoiding unstable inverse propensity weighting.
contribution: Achieves optimal confounding-robust policy selection with applications to healthcare and public policy, outperforming plug-in approaches.

problem: Optimizing LLM-based agentic systems is computationally expensive due to vast configuration space without efficient evaluation methods.
approach: Train a lightweight predictor with multi-view workflow encoding incorporating code architecture, prompts, and interaction graphs, using cross-domain unsupervised pretraining.
contribution: Agentic Predictor enables fast accurate workflow configuration selection across three domains while significantly reducing expensive trial-and-error evaluations.

problem: Video generation models fail at microscale simulation, showing violations of physical laws, temporal inconsistency, and misalignment with expert quality standards.
approach: Create MicroWorldBench rubric-based evaluation benchmark and MicroSim-10K expert-verified dataset, then train MicroVerse video model specialized for accurate microscale simulation.
contribution: Introduces the Micro-World Simulation concept with MicroVerse achieving accurate reproduction of complex microscale phenomena for biomedical and educational applications.

problem: Multi-teacher knowledge distillation for LLMs faces knowledge conflicts and high resource demands when consolidating rationales from multiple teachers.
approach: Introduce knowledge purification to consolidate teacher rationales into single coherent rationales, propose five purification methods addressing conflicts from various perspectives.
contribution: Purification methods improve distilled model performance, alleviate knowledge conflicts, and router-based methods show robust generalization for practical lightweight model deployment.

problem: Achieving both high-accuracy equilibria and low privacy budgets in polymatrix game equilibrium finding is fundamentally limited under differential privacy constraints.
approach: Establish hardness results showing impossibility of simultaneous accuracy and vanishing privacy budget, propose distributed algorithm leveraging polymatrix structure properties.
contribution: First algorithm achieving vanishing Nash gap and privacy budget simultaneously as players increase, with numerical validation.

problem: Predicting computational efficiency and model capacity for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs remains unsolved, making it difficult to design optimal MoE configurations.
approach: Introduce Efficiency Leverage metric, conduct large-scale empirical study of 300+ models up to 28B parameters, derive unified scaling laws for MoE architectures.
contribution: Scaling laws accurately predict MoE efficiency based on configuration; MoE-mini (0.85B active) matches 6.1B dense model while using 7x fewer computational resources.

problem: Hyperbolic feature spaces for RL are theoretically promising but face optimization challenges due to nonstationarity, with large-norm embeddings destabilizing gradient-based training.
approach: Analyze gradients in Poincaré ball and hyperboloid models, introduce Hyper++ with categorical value loss, feature regularization with bounded norms, and optimization-friendly hyperbolic layers.
contribution: Hyper++ guarantees stable learning on ProcGen, outperforms prior hyperbolic agents, and reduces wall-clock time by approximately 30% on Atari with Double DQN.

problem: Out-of-distribution detection methods lack consistent performance and principled theoretical foundation for leveraging neural network structure.
approach: Exploit low-rank structure of neural network gradients induced by Neural Tangent Kernel alignment, apply PCA to gradient class-means for spectral OOD detection.
contribution: GradPCA achieves more consistent OOD detection performance across benchmarks with theoretical perspective on spectral detection properties enabled by NTK alignment.

problem: VLMs struggle with precise spatial and long-horizon reasoning while PDDL planners excel at formal planning but cannot interpret visual inputs; prior work requires human-defined domain files.
approach: Use dual-VLM framework with SimVLM simulating action consequences and GenVLM iteratively refining PDDL files by comparing execution results.
contribution: VLMFP autonomously generates both problem and domain PDDL files with generalization across instances, appearances, and rules without human domain engineering.

problem: Time series anomaly detection with foundation models lacks interpretability, calibration under distribution shifts, and adaptation without retraining.
approach: Use post-hoc adaptive conformal prediction with weighted quantile bounds, learn optimal weighting parameters from past predictions while preserving guarantees.
contribution: Achieves strong performance combining simplicity, interpretability, robustness, and adaptivity while maintaining out-of-sample guarantees without model fine-tuning.

problem: Clinical decision-making requires iterative test selection and interpretation but LLMs either assume unrealistic full information availability or lack task-specific training.
approach: Model diagnosis as hypothesis-driven uncertainty-aware language agent converging toward diagnoses by requesting relevant tests, using hybrid supervised and reinforcement learning.
contribution: LA-CDM improves diagnostic performance and efficiency on MIMIC-CDM real-world dataset with explicit training for accurate hypothesis generation and efficient decision-making.

problem: Transformer-based offline RL typically learns from complete trajectories but misses high-quality subtrajectories that could improve policy learning.
approach: Propose Peak-Return Greedy Slicing to partition trajectories and extract high-quality subtrajectories using MMD-based return estimator, with adaptive history truncation at inference.
contribution: PRGS significantly improves Transformer-based offline RL performance across benchmark datasets by effectively leveraging valuable subtrajectories.

problem: Discrete diffusion models struggle to adhere to constraints during generation, limiting real-world applications requiring constrained generation.
approach: Develop Sequential Monte Carlo framework with principled importance weighting and optimal proposal design, deriving tractable weights and practical proposal approximations.
contribution: Framework enhances controllability and sample quality across synthetic tasks, language modeling, biology design, and text-to-image generation.

problem: Training set reconstruction attacks from model parameters are poorly understood theoretically and fail without prior knowledge about data distribution.
approach: Rigorously prove that without data priors, infinitely many alternative solutions exist arbitrarily far from the true training set, making reconstruction fundamentally unreliable.
contribution: Shows networks trained more extensively with stronger implicit bias are less susceptible to reconstruction attacks, reconciling privacy with generalization.

problem: Existing benchmarks lack unified evaluation for multimodal comprehension, generation, and mixed-modality generation capabilities in U-MLLMs.
approach: Create MME-Unify benchmark curating diverse tasks from 12 datasets with standardized formats and metrics, design five mixed-modality subtasks for unified evaluation.
contribution: Evaluation of 12 U-MLLMs reveals significant improvements needed in instruction following and image generation quality, providing comprehensive assessment framework.

problem: Reasoning models rely on proprietary training data with little public information, creating uncertainty about best training recipes for open-source alternatives.
approach: Create open-source reasoning datasets through systematic investigation of data generation pipeline with 1000+ controlled experiments, scale to 1.2M examples with QwQ-32B teacher.
contribution: OpenThinker3-7B achieves state-of-the-art: 53% on AIME 2025, 51% on LiveCodeBench, 54% on GPQA Diamond with public datasets and models.

problem: Synthetic EMR generation lacks adherence to rigorous clinical quality standards while merely imitating real records, limiting utility for healthcare research.
approach: Introduce LLM-CARe cyclic refinement with Critic-Adviser-Reviser collaboration across corpus, section, and document levels targeting specific granularities.
contribution: LLM-CARe significantly enhances EMR quality across all levels and improves real-world clinical tasks like diagnosis prediction without requiring real EMR text.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting degrades and becomes unstable under sparse-view conditions due to overfitting near camera and underfitting in distant areas.
approach: Introduce depth-and-density guided dropout to suppress overfitting and distance-aware fidelity enhancement for under-fitted regions, propose stability metric for robustness.
contribution: D²GS significantly improves visual quality and robustness in sparse-view conditions across multiple datasets while providing stability measurement insights.

problem: Continuous adversarial training for LLMs is costly and its theoretical mechanisms are unknown, particularly why embedding-space perturbations defend against token-space attacks.
approach: Provide first theoretical analysis of CAT based on in-context learning theory, show robustness correlates with singular values of embedding matrix, propose regularization based on this insight.
contribution: Theory explains CAT effectiveness and proposed regularization helps LLMs achieve better jailbreak robustness-utility tradeoff on real-world models.

problem: Video avatars generate fluid animations but lack authentic character essence, primarily syncing motion with audio instead of understanding emotion or intent.
approach: Use Multimodal LLMs to generate semantic textual guidance and introduce Multimodal Diffusion Transformer with Pseudo Last Frame design for robust multimodal fusion.
contribution: Achieves compelling lip-sync accuracy, video quality, motion naturalness, and semantic consistency with strong generalization to multi-person and non-human subjects.

problem: Causal discovery methods struggle with identifiability under nonlinear relationships and lack grounded asymmetry measures from observational distributions.
approach: Use Quantile Partial Effect (QPE) from conditional quantile regression as identifiability measure assuming linear span, employ Fisher Information for multivariate causal ordering.
contribution: Achieves identifiability without requiring mechanisms or Markov assumptions, effectively distinguishes causal directions through basis function tests on large bivariate datasets.

problem: Sim-to-real transfer for dexterous manipulation fails to generalize across diverse objects and conditions due to complex contact-rich dynamics creating a reality gap.
approach: Use joint-wise dynamics model that factorizes dynamics across joints and learns each joint's evolution from its profile, paired with autonomous data collection strategy.
contribution: Single policy trained in simulation generalizes to diverse real-world objects including complex shapes, high aspect ratios, and small sizes with diverse wrist orientations.

problem: LLM agents struggle with closed-loop decision-making due to static pretraining and limited temporal grounding, requiring expensive real-time interactions or brittle imitation.
approach: Learn latent world model simulating multi-step futures, score branches with uncertainty-aware value and safety gate, distill best branch into natural-language reflection conditioning policy.
contribution: DreamPhase reduces average API calls from 40 to less than 10 per episode on WebShop (4x reduction) while improving sample efficiency, safety, and cost.

problem: Long-context reasoning in LLMs lags behind other advances due to scarcity of reliable annotations and lack of programmatically verifiable reward signals.
approach: Introduce SPELL multi-role self-play RL framework with questioner-responder-verifier roles enabling label-free optimization, use automated curriculum and adaptive rewards.
contribution: SPELL shows 7.6-point pass@8 gain on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking, averaging 7.6-point improvement across long-context benchmarks without gold labels.

problem: One-step discrete generators inherit teacher bias and discrete tokens block gradient flow, preventing post-distillation refinements like adversarial training and reward fine-tuning.
approach: Replace discrete tokens with soft embeddings (expected embeddings under output distribution) providing fully differentiable continuous surrogate compatible with backbones.
contribution: Soft-DiMO achieves one-step FID of 1.56 on ImageNet-256 with GAN refinement, improving GenEval and HPS scores on text-to-image with reward fine-tuning.

problem: Zero-shot super-resolution forecasting fails because models trained on low-resolution data cannot process signals containing unseen high-frequency components above Nyquist frequency.
approach: Introduce Frequency Representation Learning with resolution-aligned representations and spectral consistency training to stabilize frequency response across resolutions.
contribution: FRL allows errors to decrease with resolution, significantly outperforming baselines within task and resolution range with modest computational overhead.

problem: Low-rank adaptation methods like LoRA underperform full fine-tuning in accuracy and convergence speed despite reducing trainable parameters.
approach: Align low-rank updates with full updates by properly projecting optimizer's first and second moments into the same low-rank subspace as LoRA.
contribution: LoFT substantially narrows performance gap with full fine-tuning, consistently outperforms LoRA without increasing inference cost and eliminates hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Self-training RL without gold labels relies on majority votes which may be spurious, hindering continual self-improvement on harder tasks.
approach: Convert absence of gold labels into learning signal through self-penalization, penalizing overconfident rollouts and low-consistency examples while preserving promising chains.
contribution: RESTRAIN achieves up to 140.7% pass@1 boost on AIME25 with only unlabeled data, nearly matching gold-label training on Qwen3-4B and OctoThinker-8B.
